subject: SLO alignment: p50/p95 targets and measurement epoch for Hosted API
messages:
From: Samir Kapoor <samir.kapoor@mirahealth.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Erin Walsh <erin.walsh@mirahealth.com>
Date: 2026-01-15T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Hosted API SLOs — aligning p50/p95 and measurement epoch

Hi Vivek,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're close to committing to Redwood for our inference layer, but legal and platform have pushed back on the SLO language. Two asks from our side before procurement can finalize:

1) Can Redwood confirm a concrete p50 / p95 latency commitment for the Hosted API for our primary model class (text generation, typical prompt length ~120 tokens)? We need explicit numbers to put in the contract.
2) How do you measure those quantiles (measurement epoch/window)? Our compliance team requires the same 24h UTC measurement epoch rather than rolling percentiles to tie to internal reporting.

We're open to a time-limited variance during our cutover (we're migrating 20% of traffic over two weeks). If you can outline a short-term mitigation or fallback plan and a reporting cadence, that will help unblock procurement.

Attached is a short list of the latency targets Mira would like to see in the contract.

Appreciate your help — Samir

--
Samir Kapoor
Head of Platform, MiraHealth
samir.kapoor@mirahealth.com
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Samir Kapoor <samir.kapoor@mirahealth.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-01-15T11:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API SLOs — aligning p50/p95 and measurement epoch

Hi Samir — thanks, and great question. I wanted to give a concise, engineering-backed response and loop in Irene (SRE) and Rishi (Contracts) to get eyes on measurement and legal implications. High-level:

- Baseline commitment we can firm up in a Hosted API enterprise addendum (subject to traffic profile): p50 = 45ms, p95 = 210ms for 0-512 token requests under our standard runtime profile in eu-west regions.
- Measurement: our default is rolling quantiles computed over a 7-day window to smooth transient bursts. We can, however, align to a 24h UTC epoch for contractual reporting if Mira requires that (we'll mark it as the canonical measurement epoch).
- Temporary cutover variance: we'll accept a 30-day transitional variance where we commit to the canonical epoch but allow for a twice-daily operational carveout window if you experience a planned migration spike. During the variance we will provide daily CSV reports of raw latency samples and an incident channel.

Two asks back to you:
1) Please confirm traffic mix (inference QPS and percent of long-context requests >512 tokens) so we can validate the numbers.
2) Confirm you accept a short remediation SLA (30 days) tied to our runbook — if p95 misses persist beyond that we propose a credit or model-tier fallback.

I'll prepare a short playbook and a sample report (Irene, can you attach an example snapshot?) and Rishi will draft the contract language for the 24h epoch clause and the 30-day variance.

Best,
Vivek

--
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Samir Kapoor <samir.kapoor@mirahealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-01-18T08:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API SLOs — aligning p50/p95 and measurement epoch

Samir / Vivek — attaching a sample evidence snapshot (evidence_kpi_snapshot.json) and a short playbook (proposed_playbook.pdf) so you can see how we compute quantiles and what raw outputs look like. Summary of how we measure and what we recommend: 

- Measurement details:
  * We capture per-request server-side tail latency at the token-completion boundary (includes queueing + exec time).
  * Quantiles computed using streaming T-Digest on per-region clusters.
  * Canonical reporting options: rolling-7d (default) or fixed 24h UTC epoch (contractual).

- Recommended contractual numbers (eu):
  * p50: 45ms
  * p95: 210ms
  Notes: those numbers assume the standard model shard and the median sequence length you quoted (~120 tokens). Long-context workloads will shift p95 — please flag if >10% of requests exceed 512 tokens.

- Temporary variance & mitigation playbook (for migration):
  1) 30-day variance window starting on cutover date.
  2) Twice-daily snapshots sent to Mira (CSV + raw samples).
  3) Automated fallback policy: traffic >95th percentile latency routed to a smaller, lower-latency variant for a configurable fraction of requests.
  4) We will run a pre-cutover canary for 48 hours (10% traffic) with live dashboards and a post-mortem within 72 hours if there are overruns.

If you confirm traffic profile I can include the expected small-change delta for p95 under your distribution.

Regards,
Irene Choi
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.com

Date: 2026-01-20T15:48:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API SLOs — aligning p50/p95 and measurement epoch (Agreement & next steps)

Samir / Erin — following up to lock this in so procurement can finish the paperwork. Agreed items below (we'll put formal language in the addendum):

- Canonical latency commitments (eu region, standard model class, median request ~120 tokens): p50 = 45ms, p95 = 210ms.
- Measurement epoch: 24h UTC epoch will be the contractual reporting window. We will also compute rolling-7d for operational visibility.
- Transitional variance: 30 days from cutover start. During the variance Redwood will:
  * Provide daily CSVs of raw latency samples and twice-daily summary snapshots.
  * Run a 48-hour 10% canary prior to full cutover.
  * Enable automatic fallback to a lower-latency model variant if p95 breaches by more than 15% for a sustained 3-hour window.
- Reporting & governance: daily ops check-ins during the 30-day variance, weekly thereafter for the remainder of onboarding.

Next steps for Mira: please reply with a) confirmed cutover start date window, and b) traffic profile (expected average QPS and % of requests >512 tokens). Rishi, please attach the contractual addendum draft once ready. I've attached the workbook Mira sent and our evidence snapshot for reference.

If that looks right, I'll ask legal to bake the 24h epoch clause and the 30-day variance into the enterprise addendum and will schedule a standing 15-min check-in for the variance period.

Thanks — looking forward to getting you onboarded.

Vivek
--
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
